name: Togail Troí
text: Togail Troí is the medieval Irish tale of the fall of Troy. The title means the destruction of Troy. It ranks as the best loved and most far-reaching classical story in Ireland. The text has a long and layered history. An early Irish list of tales already names it. It is the only classical piece kept in the great codex called the Book of Leinster. The first rendering came in the tenth century. The oldest surviving copy dates to the eleventh. Togail Troí is a free retelling. The bare tale of Dares is stretched out and told in the native manner of the Ulster sagas. Mac Eoin set out three prose forms and one rare verse form. A later scholar offered a different grouping. Every copy except one Dublin manuscript belongs to a shared line. The copies differ by how far the text was expanded. The longest form takes in long passages from the poems of Publius Papinius Statius. It adds a sequel about the rebuilding of the city. Printing every form is the key to seeing how Ireland received the classical tradition.

okr.objective: Document the Irish saga Togail Troí and its reception of the Trojan War story.
key_results: Record it as the most popular and influential classical tale in Ireland
List the three main prose editions and one verse edition
Show that only this classical text survives in the Book of Leinster
okr.evidence: The source describes the text as the centre of the classical corpus in Ireland, named in an early tale list and surviving in the Book of Leinster.
